- A01 shows the mirror image: not observed earlier, it runs in about 50 in 100 traces in the later window (about one occurrence per trace, repeated in about 28 in 100). [OCC001, POS001]
- A01 and A03 never share a trace in either window: earlier, about 45 in 100 traces contained A03 without A01; later, about 50 in 100 contained A01 without A03. [REL001]
- The two occupy the same place in the flow: A03's median position was about 0.39 of the trace earlier, A01's is about 0.38 later, with nearly identical quartiles (roughly 0.17–0.62 in both windows). [POS002, POS001]
- The connections moved with them: of A09's observed outgoing transitions, about 52 in 100 went to A03 earlier while about 55 in 100 go to A01 later; A11's transitions to A03 (about 22 in 100) became transitions to A01 (about 18 in 100). [DIR003, DIR004]
- A01's later outgoing profile closely copies A03's earlier one: mainly to A11 (about 46 in 100, previously 45), then A12, A10 and A09 at about 15–16 in 100 each (previously about 14–18). [DIR001, DIR002]
- A03's former partners now pair with A01 instead: A03 co-occurred with A11, A09, A10 and A12 in about 28–45 in 100 traces earlier and never later, while A01 co-occurs with each of them in about 35–50 in 100 traces later, with similarly mixed orders (interleaving in about 23–32 in 100). The same handover appears with A05: co-occurrence with A03 (about 38 in 100) became co-occurrence with A01 (about 44 in 100). [REL010, REL005, REL008, REL003, REL009, REL004, REL011, REL006, REL007, REL002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A01 was introduced in place of A03 and took over its role in the flow. Earlier, A03 ran in about 45 in 100 traces and A01 was not observed; later, A03 is no longer observed and A01 runs in about 50 in 100 traces at the same relative position. A01 also inherits A03's neighbourhood: A09's handover flipped from A03 to A01, and A01 now feeds A11, A12, A10 and A09 in nearly the same shares A03 did, while the two activities never occur in the same trace. [OCC001, OCC002, POS001, POS002, REL001, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]

The hypothesis is shown directly and consistently: relational and positional evidence captures the substitution itself, not only its side effects, all nineteen qualifying items describe the same rewiring, and the volume of flagged differences (19 items against roughly 0.33 expected by chance across the 67 tested control-flow units) is far beyond what random re-splits of these windows produce; the non-zero sides of the profiles rest on 56–203 observations each. [OCC001, OCC002, POS001, POS002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011]

Limitations: the evidence cannot rule out that A01 is a re-labelled A03 rather than a distinct new step, since the activity codes are anonymous and the windows are finite samples; and zero participation only means an activity was not observed in that window, so A03 could still occur outside these samples. [OCC002, POS002]

Other differences: in the later window, low-share transitions (about 1–4 in 100 of the relevant source's outgoing transitions) link A01 and A11 to A13, A15 and A02, mirroring low-share edges that A03 and A11 already had earlier; these minor edges are not part of the main hypothesis. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
